subject: social spider colony
title: Thousands of Spiders Share One Web and Hunt in Perfect Step

scenes.text: Thousands of spiders share one web. And they hunt in step.
Anelosimus eximius, in the rainforests of South America. Colonies of thousands, webs several meters across, each spider about a quarter inch long.
Together they take prey up to 700 times the weight of one spider. Moths, grasshoppers, things that would eat a lone spider.
In 2022 scientists filmed how. The whole group moves, then freezes, all at once. Pauses of about half a second.
Why? Their own footsteps shake the web and drown out the prey. Freezing together lets every spider hear where dinner is struggling. Nobody leads.
Thirty spiders, one rhythm, no leader. The moth never had a chance.

description:
Thousands of spiders share one web the size of a small house, and they hunt in perfect synchrony.
Anelosimus eximius colonies in South America can hold thousands of quarter-inch spiders and catch prey up to 700 times the weight of a single spider. A 2022 PNAS study filmed in French Guiana showed hunting groups averaging 30 spiders moving and freezing in unison, with stops of roughly half a second, so their own footsteps don't drown out the vibrations of the struggling prey. There is no leader; each spider reacts to the web.
Would you rather face one big spider or a thousand small ones that work together?
first_comment: Of about 50,000 spider species, only around 20 live in permanent colonies, and only one or two hunt in packs like this. Which animal team-up impresses you most?
